specification.problem: Grover search over a classical database D[0..N-1] of m-bit words, N=2^n, to find an address i with D[i]=w, using an oracle built from a QRAM-like lookup (address-controlled X gates) with compute, mark and uncompute steps.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny explicit instance, e.g. n=2, m=2, M=1, with the database and target known classically at build time. Includes load, mark via a |-> flag, uncompute, diffusion, iteration count and index readout. Paper-specific details beyond the abstract (exact gate-level QRAM design, resource counts, generalization to multiple matches or large databases) are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: classical database word at address i
number of addresses i with D[i]=w

symbols.domain: unitary on index and data registers

equations.label: QRAM load
equations.description: Coherent read of the classical memory, implemented as X on data qubit j controlled on the index register equal to i. Controls for 0 bits of i are flipped by X gates around the mcx.
equations.abstract_quote: The oracle contains a kind of quantumly accessible classical memory, which stores the database.
equations.justification: The abstract says the oracle contains quantumly accessible classical memory storing the database; the address-controlled X realization is an assumed implementation.
assumptions: Lookup uses only X, mcx gates
Each gate toggles bits, so U_D is self-inverse

equations.label: Flag phase marking
equations.latex: \mathrm{MCX}_{R\to f}\,|x\rangle_R|-\rangle_f=(-1)^{[x=w]}|x\rangle_R|-\rangle_f,\quad \text{with X on data bits where }w_j=0\text{ before and after}
equations.description: Compare the data register to w via X conjugation, then an mcx onto the flag qubit in |->, giving a phase kickback.
equations.justification: Standard phase-kickback marking, proposed as the oracle's comparison step.
assumptions: Flag qubit prepared in |-> via X then H

equations.label: Clean oracle
equations.description: Load, mark, then uncompute so the data register returns to zero and the oracle acts as a phase oracle on the index.
equations.justification: Compute-mark-uncompute follows from eq_1 and eq_2; the abstract only proposes a circuit implementation of the Grover oracle.

equations.label: Diffusion operator
equations.latex: G=\left(2|s\rangle\langle s|-I\right)O,\quad |s\rangle=H^{\otimes n}|0\rangle^{n},\quad 2|s\rangle\langle s|-I=H^{\otimes n}X^{\otimes n}\,\mathrm{C}^{n-1}Z\,X^{\otimes n}H^{\otimes n}\ \text{(up to global phase)}
equations.description: Grover iteration applied to the index register.
equations.justification: Standard Grover diffusion; the reflection is equal up to a global sign.
assumptions: n>=2 for the multi-controlled Z, or use plain Z for n=1

equations.label: Iteration count and success probability
equations.description: Number of iterations and resulting probability of measuring a marked address.
equations.justification: Textbook Grover analysis. For N=4, M=1, R=1 and P=1.

registers.name: index
registers.role: address register, searched over; qubit i is the i-th bit of the address (little-endian)

registers.name: data
registers.role: QRAM output word register, returned to |0> after each oracle

specification.initial_state: index qubits H^{\otimes n}|0>, data |0>^m, flag |-> (X then H). Total n+m+1 qubits, plus an optional mcx ancilla.

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition on the index register and the flag in |->.
Load: apply the address-controlled X gates for every i and every bit j with D[i]_j=1.
Mark: X on data bits where w_j=0, mcx from data to flag, undo the X gates.
Uncompute: repeat the load step so the data register returns to |0>, giving the clean oracle O.
Apply diffusion on the index register. Repeat steps 2-5 R times.

specification.measurement: Measure only the n index qubits, with measure(i,i) for index qubit i. In Qiskit counts keys the last character is classical bit 0, so bits[::-1][i] is index qubit i.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Take the most frequent bitstring, reverse it to little-endian, and read the integer address i. Optionally check D[i]=w classically.
assumptions: Smallest instance: n=2, m=2, M=1, with D and w chosen so that the target is unique
D and w are known at build time
The oracle is a standard-gate construction with no black box, and one oracle use is one query per iteration
